  "source": "web_research",
  "core_problem": "Reasoning models' thinking-phase KV caches persist throughout answer generation despite containing massive exploratory, backtracking, and redundant content that is irrelevant once conclusions are reached. The ideal importance oracle — attention from generated answer tokens back to thinking tokens — is inaccessible at the `</think>` boundary: no answer tokens have been generated yet. Progressive methods score token importance using only the available prefix at each generation step, unable to exploit the complete thinking trace. DynTS (arXiv:2601.18383) trains a lightweight MLP predictor to approximate answer-to-thinking attention during generation, requiring ~7K domain-specific labeled examples; the authors explicitly note it is limited to mathematical reasoning. Expected Attention (arXiv:2510.00636) estimates future query importance in closed form by assuming hidden states follow Gaussian distributions — a training-free statistical approximation that avoids actual future queries but relies on Gaussian distributional assumptions and position-averaged RoPE embeddings. No existing training-free method uses the complete thinking trace context to score thinking-token importance via explicitly instantiated query vectors before the first answer token is generated.",
  "opportunity": "The `</think>` boundary token (shared by both DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3 reasoning families, and configurable as `reasoning_end_str` in vLLM deployments) creates a natural one-shot compression trigger with a decisive advantage: the completed thinking trace is available for full-trace importance scoring before any answer generation begins. A single batched pre-RoPE attention pass seeded from the final N=128 conclusion tokens of the completed thinking trace accumulates per-position importance scores across all layers before the first answer token is generated. These conclusion tokens — the synthesis and convergence phase at the end of thinking, where reasoning models explicitly prepare their answer — serve as the strongest available proxy for answer-phase queries: they attend over the same completed trace, semantically anticipate the forthcoming answer, and yield exact attention scores rather than statistical estimates. Critically, this is not oracle computation (the true oracle requires actual answer tokens unavailable at the boundary), but it is a qualitatively superior approximation compared to both progressive prefix-only methods (which cannot see the complete trace) and distributional estimators (which rely on Gaussian assumptions). The three-way differentiation: DynTS trains an MLP to predict answer-to-thinking attention — a learned approximation limited to math; Expected Attention estimates future queries via Gaussian distributional properties — a statistical approximation requiring no instantiated queries; RIC instantiates explicit conclusion-token queries from the completed thinking trace — an exact attention computation over the full trace requiring no training and no distributional assumptions. Aggressive compression to ≥90% KV eviction is the appropriate headline target: ThinKV achieves <5% retention near-losslessly (1.3% at <4% accuracy drop on AIME), R-KV achieves 10% retention at ~100% baseline accuracy training-free via progressive scoring. Full-trace conclusion-phase scoring provides stronger importance signal than either method's progressive prefix-only approach, motivating equally aggressive eviction budgets with superior Pareto quality.",
  "landscape": "DynTS (Jan 2026, arXiv:2601.18383) — the closest conceptual competitor — trains a lightweight Importance Predictor MLP at the final layer using ~7K MATH samples (MSE on oracle answer-to-thinking attention weights), then applies it incrementally during decoding to score thinking tokens without seeing the complete answer. Achieves 3.32–5.73× KV reduction (17–30% retention) but is explicitly limited to mathematical reasoning by its training data. ThinKV (Oct 2025, arXiv:2510.01290, ICLR 2026 Oral) decomposes chain-of-thought into reasoning/execution/transition segments via attention sparsity and applies hybrid quantization–eviction progressively, achieving near-lossless accuracy with <5% KV cache (1.3% at <4% drop on AIME with AceReason-14B) and 5.8× throughput on AIME/LiveCodeBench — sets the compression SOTA bar. Expected Attention (Oct 2025, arXiv:2510.00636, submitted ICLR 2026 OpenReview) — training-free, computes expected attention scores in closed form by modeling hidden states as Gaussian-distributed; queries (linear transforms of hidden states) inherit this distribution, enabling analytical importance estimation via the moment-generating function (ẑᵢ = exp(μ̄_q^T k_i/√d + k_i^T Σ̄_q k_i/2d)) without materializing future tokens or actual query vectors; position-averaged over T=512 future positions for RoPE compatibility. Achieves 12× decoding compression while preserving reasoning capability; also released KVPress library with 20+ compression techniques. RIC differentiation: Expected Attention relies on Gaussian distributional assumptions and position-averaged RoPE; RIC instantiates actual conclusion-token query vectors from the completed thinking trace, yielding exact attention scores over the full trace with zero distributional assumptions. Crystal-KV (Jan 2026, arXiv:2601.16986) uses an answer-first LRFU policy throughout generation — still prefix-only. ForesightKV (Feb 2026, arXiv:2602.03203) uses SL+RL to learn step-level long-term importance predictions, consistently outperforming prior methods at 50% cache budget on AIME2024/2025, but requires training overhead and operates during generation. R-KV (May 2025, arXiv:2505.24133, NeurIPS 2025) achieves ~100% baseline accuracy with 10% KV cache and 105% baseline accuracy with 16% KV cache via redundancy-aware joint importance-eviction scoring — training-free, progressive. LongFlow (Mar 2026, arXiv:2603.11504) integrates FlashAttention with current-query importance estimation in a single fused kernel, achieving 11.8× throughput and 80% compression with minimal accuracy loss — general long-output reasoning compression. LookaheadKV (Mar 2026, arXiv:2603.10899, ICLR 2026) trains parameter-efficient modules to predict future token importance during prefilling, reducing eviction cost by 14.5× over draft-based methods — learned future-importance prediction during prefilling rather than generation. LASER-KV / 'More Than a Quick Glance' (Feb 2026, arXiv:2602.02199) proposes block-wise layer-accumulated selection to overcome the greedy prefix-only bias, maintaining performance on Babilong at 128K where prior methods degrade 15–30%. Neural Garbage Collection (Apr 2026, arXiv:2604.18002) trains models end-to-end via RL to self-evict during generation — requires model fine-tuning, incremental not boundary-triggered. TriAttention (Apr 2026, arXiv:2604.04921) achieves 10.7× KV compression on AIME2025 via stable pre-RoPE Q/K concentration around fixed non-zero centers, which causes distance-preference expressible as a trigonometric series — operates throughout generation. KVSculpt (Mar 2026, arXiv:2603.27819) optimizes unconstrained KV pairs in continuous space via L-BFGS and least squares to preserve per-layer attention behavior — distillation framing relevant to RIC's Section 5 extension. Hold Onto That Thought (NeurIPS Workshop 2025, arXiv:2512.12008) provides empirical evidence that full-context importance estimates substantially outperform prefix-only estimates — foundational motivation for boundary-triggered scoring. Bottlenecked Transformers (May 2025, arXiv:2505.16950) also trigger KV processing at reasoning-step boundaries — specifically at every newline-delimited step throughout generation, using a trained Cache Processor (auxiliary Transformer) to perform non-causal in-place KV rewrites that consolidate recent entries; it requires supervised training of the auxiliary module alongside the main model and yields no net memory reduction (in-place restructuring, not eviction). RIC differs on all three axes: zero training required, single one-shot trigger at the semantically motivated reasoning-answer boundary, and aggressive memory reduction via eviction. Lookahead Q-Cache (LAQ, May 2025, arXiv:2505.20334) addresses the same prefill-scoring mismatch problem by generating low-cost pseudo lookahead queries to approximate decoding-phase queries during prefill — a training-free approach. RIC applies the analogous intuition at the reasoning-answer boundary: the final N tokens of the completed thinking trace serve as a naturally arising, model-generated query proxy rather than a synthetic pseudo-query, and the scoring is exact (instantiated query vectors) rather than approximate. RIC is the first training-free method to use explicitly instantiated conclusion-token query vectors over the complete thinking trace at the reasoning-answer boundary, requiring no predictor training, no distributional assumptions, and incurring zero per-step overhead during thinking generation.",
  "approach": "Upon detecting the `</think>` boundary token, RIC performs a one-shot Retrospective Importance Cascade: the final N=128 conclusion tokens of the completed thinking trace serve as seed queries for a single batched attention pass over the full thinking-phase KV cache. **Pre-RoPE computation**: The attention pass is computed in pre-RoPE space to prevent RoPE-induced positional distance bias — without this correction, conclusion-token queries at position ~20K would spuriously suppress attention scores for early-but-important thinking tokens at position ~0 due to RoPE's distance-decaying cosine schedule, biasing importance scoring against the opening context of the thinking trace regardless of actual content importance. (TriAttention independently motivates pre-RoPE computation for a different reason — Q/K concentration stability — providing convergent support for the pre-RoPE design choice.) **Pre-RoPE implementation**: At the `</think>` boundary, we apply inverse RoPE to the already-cached post-RoPE thinking-phase key tensors (`K_unrot = R_{−p}(K_rot)`, implemented as element-wise rotation by negated positions, identical in FLOPs cost to a single RoPE forward pass) and compute conclusion-token queries without positional embedding application; both the temporary pre-RoPE key buffer and the de-rotated query vectors are held only for the duration of the importance scoring pass and immediately discarded thereafter, incurring zero additional key memory overhead during the thinking phase itself. Per-position importance scores are accumulated across all layers and heads via depth-weighted max-pooling, completing before the first answer token is generated. **Conclusion token validity**: SnapKV (arXiv:2404.14469) establishes the direct methodological precedent for this scoring strategy: using the last L=16–64 tokens of an input sequence as an observation window yields query distributions closely aligned with subsequent generation, because the final completed tokens of a sequence best anticipate what follows. RIC applies this principle at the reasoning-answer boundary rather than the prompt-generation boundary. Behavioral evidence that reasoning models enter a structurally distinct synthesis phase before `</think>`: thinking traces exhibit an identifiable terminal phase characterized by self-assertion and summary consolidation behavior (arXiv:2509.13758 shows 17.48% of traces end in a Self-Assertion + Summary pattern), and hierarchical FSM analysis identifies a distinct 'final-conclusion' closure state terminating reasoning traces (arXiv:2510.22437); attention-head trajectory analysis reveals reasoning-focused heads follow diagonal trajectories that terminate near reflection tokens (arXiv:2509.23676), consistent with convergence toward answer preparation. These citations support the conclusion-token hypothesis; the N ablation (N ∈ {64, 128, 256} plus a matched-budget random mid-trace baseline) provides primary empirical validation by testing whether conclusion tokens outperform randomly sampled thinking tokens as query proxies.\n\nThese scores drive tiered compression with **90% eviction as the headline configuration** (90% evicted, 7% INT4 retained, 3% FP16 retained = 10% total nominal retention), with **80% eviction as the conservative variant** (80% evicted, 15% INT4, 5% FP16 = 20% total nominal retention). **Effective memory comparison (bit-normalized)**: At the 90% eviction headline, RIC's mixed-precision tiering yields **76 effective bits per KV slot** (3%×16 + 7%×4 = 48 + 28 bits), compared to R-KV's 10% full-precision retention at **160 effective bits per KV slot** (10%×16 bits) — a **52% reduction in effective KV memory** at equal nominal eviction rate, achieved through mixed-precision tiering rather than additional eviction. RIC's 3% FP16 + 7% INT4 configuration thus achieves lower effective memory than R-KV's lossless 10% full-precision configuration while targeting comparable accuracy through full-trace scoring rather than progressive prefix-only scoring. The 80% conservative variant serves as a quality floor demonstrating robust performance at a relaxed budget. Answer-phase KV pairs are never touched. The eviction rate (70%, 80%, 90%), N (64, 128, 256), and depth-weighting scheme are swept in ablations. **Boundary robustness**: Primary detection matches the `</think>` token, which is shared across both DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3 reasoning families and configurable via vLLM's `reasoning_end_str`. For models lacking explicit markers (distillations that produce empty thinking blocks or omit the tag entirely), a fallback entropy-shift detector monitors per-token generation entropy across a sliding window; a sustained drop exceeding 1.0 nat over 20 consecutive tokens signals the reasoning-to-conclusion transition and triggers RIC. Empty thinking blocks (<256 tokens) are detected and bypassed to avoid overhead. **Latency quantification**: The boundary compression step is measured wall-clock for 8B and 32B models at 20K and 50K thinking-token lengths; preliminary analysis estimates <10ms for typical sequences (bandwidth-limited KV cache read: ~2–6 GB at 2 TB/s on A100 for 20K–50K tokens) — reported as absolute latency and as a percentage of total generation time, expected to be <1% overhead. **Comparison table** (Table 1): RIC vs. DynTS (trained MLP, incremental, math-only), Expected Attention (training-free, Gaussian distributional estimation, not boundary-triggered), ForesightKV (SL+RL, per-step, general), ThinKV (training-free, progressive, <5% retention), R-KV (training-free, progressive, 10% retention at 100% accuracy), LookaheadKV (trained, prefilling-phase), Crystal-KV (training-free, LRFU), Neural GC (RL fine-tuning, incremental), Bottlenecked Transformers (trained Cache Processor, periodic per-step boundary, no memory reduction) — columns: training required, scoring mechanism (learned / statistical / exact-instantiated), full-trace context used, compression rate, boundary-triggered, net memory reduction, benchmark scope. **Results framing**: The paper's strongest claim is that RIC achieves a comparable accuracy-efficiency Pareto to ThinKV (which requires attention-sparsity-based CoT segmentation to identify reasoning/execution/transition token categories) while requiring only the `</think>` boundary event and no structural decomposition of the thinking trace — simpler and more broadly applicable. Against progressive methods (R-KV, Expected Attention), RIC's advantage is that full-trace scoring from conclusion-token queries provides a stronger importance signal than prefix-only scoring from any mid-thinking query, directly manifesting as higher retained accuracy at equal compression budgets. This framing should be made explicit in the results section as the organizing Pareto claim. **Section 5 extension — distillation variant** (one paragraph, not a co-equal contribution): A lightweight MLP trained on offline RIC importance scores predicts per-position importance from local attention statistics, amortizing the boundary pass cost at inference time. Unlike DynTS's predictor — trained on per-step answer-to-thinking oracle signals and limited to mathematical reasoning — this variant's teacher signal is full-trace conclusion-phase RIC scores, enabling cross-domain transfer (following the KVSculpt distillation paradigm). This is framed as a future direction; the core paper's training-free property is the primary differentiator and the distillation variant is explicitly marked as not requiring additional experiments for the main submission. **Cross-family timeline management**: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B and -32B results are fully finalized by day 12 of the auto-research timeline. Qwen3-32B-Thinking cross-family evaluation is treated as a robustness bonus: it proceeds in parallel only after the entropy-shift fallback is validated on at least one distilled-model holdout (by day 10) and 8B/32B DeepSeek results confirm robust performance. If Qwen3 results require a revision cycle, they are reported as a supplementary robustness check rather than a main-paper claim. **Evaluation**: AIME2024/2025, AMC10/12, MATH-500 (math reasoning); HumanEval and LiveCodeBench (coding, using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B); LongBench and RULER (long-context understanding); MT-Bench (instruction following) — reported as accuracy-vs-KV-budget Pareto curves against ThinKV, DynTS, Expected Attention, ForesightKV, R-KV, LongFlow, LookaheadKV, and Neural GC baselines on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B/32B and Qwen3-32B-Thinking.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 4)
Issues: ["MODERATE — Pareto framing remains imprecise in a way that will draw reviewer fire. The proposal claims 'comparable Pareto to ThinKV without requiring CoT segmentation,' but ThinKV's headline is 5% retention vs. RIC's 10% retention. 'Comparable' at different retention levels is confusing. The correct framing is: 'At equal retention budgets (e.g., both at 10%), RIC should outperform ThinKV because full-trace context provides stronger importance signal than ThinKV's prefix-only progressive scoring' — this is the head-to-head claim that actually needs to be made explicit, and if experiments confirm it, is a stronger result than the current framing. If ThinKV at 10% matches RIC at 10%, the 'no CoT segmentation' advantage must be the primary claim, not 'comparable Pareto.'", "MINOR-MODERATE — R-KV (arXiv:2505.24133) explicitly observes that 'many cached tokens selected by attention-based methods show repetitions related to self-reflection and conclusion' and treats this as evidence of redundancy to evict. RIC uses conclusion tokens as QUERY vectors (not keys to retain), but this observation raises a subtle concern: if conclusion tokens are self-referential and attend to recent/local tokens rather than globally important early reasoning steps, conclusion-token QUERIES could bias importance scoring toward recency rather than global relevance. The proposal cites behavioral evidence that conclusion tokens exhibit synthesis behavior (arXiv:2509.13758, etc.) but does not address R-KV's contrary observation. The paper should include one sentence acknowledging this and explaining why the query role (attending FROM conclusion tokens) differs from the key role (being attended TO by other tokens), as these are distinct properties.", "MINOR — ThinKV's 'ICLR 2026 Oral' status cannot be verified from the arXiv page (arXiv:2510.01290 does not list conference acceptance). If this status is incorrect, EMNLP reviewers familiar with ICLR 2026 proceedings will flag it. Change to 'ICLR 2026' or 'arXiv:2510.01290' without the Oral qualifier unless the acceptance is independently confirmed.", "MINOR — At the `</think>` boundary, applying inverse RoPE to cached post-RoPE keys creates a temporary pre-RoPE key buffer held concurrently with the original KV cache, causing a 2× peak key memory spike for the duration of the scoring pass. For a 32B model at 50K thinking tokens, this is approximately 6-7 GB of additional key memory (50K × 64 layers × 8 KV heads × 128 dim × 2 bytes). The proposal correctly notes 'zero additional key memory overhead during the thinking phase itself' but does not quantify this boundary-moment peak, which affects deployment feasibility on memory-constrained H100 configurations. Add one sentence: 'At the boundary, inverse-RoPE computation transiently doubles peak key memory for approximately T_boundary seconds (measured at ~X ms); for 32B models at 50K thinking tokens, this is approximately Y GB, within A100/H100 capacity.'"]
Feedback: This proposal has comprehensively addressed all Round 3 issues: Bottlenecked Transformers is cited, inverse-RoPE implementation is specified, conclusion-token behavioral evidence is provided, and memory normalization is explicit. The remaining gap before pass quality is primarily one framing correction and one omitted counter-evidence acknowledgment.

Based on the search results for arXiv paper 2505.24133, here's what I found:

R-KV is a novel method specifically targeting redundant tokens in reasoning models, focusing on redundancy-aware KV cache compression.

## Key Problem and Redundancy Issue

Reasoning models have demonstrated impressive performance in self-reflection and chain-of-thought reasoning, but they often produce excessively long outputs, leading to prohibitively large key-value (KV) caches during inference. More specifically, outputs from current reasoning models, especially during complex chain-of-thought generation, are fundamentally marked by pervasive redundancy, with superfluous content including unnecessary reflections, iterative re-evaluations, and verbose self-dialogue.

Over half of the tokens in reasoning chains contribute minimally to task performance, indicating that repetitive self-verification steps or intermediate calculations could be substantially reduced.

## The Redundancy Challenge

Standard KV-cache compression methods that rely on simple attention-based importance filtering often fail because the repetitive sections generate high attention signals for themselves. Naively pruning tokens with "low attention weight" may remove crucial but scattered bits of reasoning, or over-retain duplicative self-reflections that appear to have high attention, which motivates exploring redundancy-aware compression strategies that selectively retain "important and non-repetitive context" during decoding.

## Performance Results

R-KV preserves nearly 100% of the full KV cache performance using only 10% of the KV cache, substantially outperforming existing KV cache baselines which reach only 60% of the performance, and even achieves 105% of full KV cache performance with 16% of the KV cache.

R-KV is a novel method specifically targeting redundant tokens in reasoning models, focusing on redundancy-aware KV cache compression.

## Key Problem and Redundancy Issue

Reasoning models have demonstrated impressive performance in self-reflection and chain-of-thought reasoning, but they often produce excessively long outputs, leading to prohibitively large key-value (KV) caches during inference. More specifically, outputs from current reasoning models, especially during complex chain-of-thought generation, are fundamentally marked by pervasive redundancy, with superfluous content including unnecessary reflections, iterative re-evaluations, and verbose self-dialogue.

Over half of the tokens in reasoning chains contribute minimally to task performance, indicating that repetitive self-verification steps or intermediate calculations could be substantially reduced.

## The Redundancy Challenge

Standard KV-cache compression methods that rely on simple attention-based importance filtering often fail because the repetitive sections generate high attention signals for themselves. Naively pruning tokens with "low attention weight" may remove crucial but scattered bits of reasoning, or over-retain duplicative self-reflections that appear to have high attention, which motivates exploring redundancy-aware compression strategies that selectively retain "important and non-repetitive context" during decoding.

## Performance Results

R-KV preserves nearly 100% of the full KV cache performance using only 10% of the KV cache, substantially outperforming existing KV cache baselines which reach only 60% of the performance, and even achieves 105% of full KV cache performance with 16% of the KV cache.
